note: trimmed to the commands council-flow uses

examples: orca automations create --name "Daily review" --trigger daily --prompt "Review open changes" --provider codex
orca automations create --name "Weekday triage" --trigger "0 9 * * 1-5" --prompt "Triage issues" --provider claude --repo my-repo
orca automations create --name "PR review" --trigger hourly --precheck "gh pr list --json number -q .[0].number" --prompt "Review requested PRs" --provider codex
orca automations create --name "Docs pass" --trigger daily --prompt "Tidy the docs" --provider claude --extra-agent-args="--model opus --effort high --add-dir docs"
notes: Trigger accepts hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, a 5-field cron expression, or an RRULE string.
When --repo is omitted, the CLI uses the enclosing Orca worktree when one can be resolved from cwd.

Use --project, or --project-host-setup, to run on a specific project host setup. --project takes the project id or the display name from `orca project list`, and --host is only needed when the project is set up on more than one host.
--host takes local, ssh:<target-id>, runtime:<environment-id>, or the bare host name `orca host list` prints for any of them.
Use --source-context with a JSON TaskSourceContext when task/provider data should come from a specific host/account; pass null on edit to clear it.

Use --workspace to run in an existing worktree. With --repo or a project target, the automation creates a new worktree per run; with no target, a local create runs in the current Orca worktree unless you pass --workspace-mode new-per-run.

Use --setup run|skip for repository setup on new-per-run automations. Explicit choices override the repository setup policy and need a host running current Orca. When omitted on create, no choice is saved; current Orca skips setup.
Use --precheck to run a command only before scheduled runs; exit code 0 continues, any other exit, error, or timeout skips the run.
Use --precheck-timeout <seconds> to set the time limit (default 60 seconds). Skips appear in Orca run history and orca automations runs --id <automation-id> as skipped_precheck.
Run now in Orca and orca automations run intentionally bypass the precheck so you can test or override the scheduled condition.
Use --reuse-session only with existing-workspace automations to submit later runs to the previous live automation session when it is still available. Use --fresh-session to disable reuse.

Use --extra-agent-args="--model opus --effort high" to add arguments after the host's default agent Arguments on each fresh run. Only model, effort, and a few safe options are accepted (Antigravity, Claude, Codex, CodeBuddy, Cursor, Grok, OMP, Pi); extras cannot be combined with --reuse-session. On edit, --extra-agent-args= clears them.

commands.summary: Read Linear issue context for agents
Ask the coordinator a question; Orca wakes you with the answer
notes: From a worker, a new question goes to its coordinator and ask returns at once: end your turn, and Orca wakes you with the answer as mail. A worker that already finished waits for the answer instead. --wait and --resume block until the answer instead; --timeout-ms accepts 1 to 1800000 ms per wait (default 600000 = 10 minutes, max 30 minutes), and a timeout leaves the question pending.

commands.usage:
orca orchestration check [--terminal <handle>] [--run <run_id>] [--ack <delivery_id>] [--unread | --peek | --all] [--types <type,...>] [--format] [--wait] [--timeout-ms <n>] [--retry-request <id>] [--json]
  default: return the bound Run's oldest unread FIFO batch and mark it handled.
  --ack: optional; acknowledges a batch from an older Orca that does not mark it.
  --peek: return only unread messages without marking them read.
  --all: return recent messages for the handle; does not mark read.
  --wait: block until a matching message arrives or --timeout-ms expires.
          Emits JSON keepalive lines to stderr every 15s so the caller can
          tell the process is alive. `_keepalive` is unrelated to heartbeat
          messages; `_heartbeat` remains as a deprecated compatibility alias.
          Filter with `jq "select(._keepalive|not)"` when merging streams.
notes: On Windows PowerShell, quote comma-separated type filters, e.g. --types "worker_done,escalation".

--types is the wake condition for --wait; a returned Delivery is always the whole FIFO batch, so it is never filtered by type. Without --wait it has no effect on consuming checks. Only --peek and --all filter their rows.
--format renders the returned rows as local text only; it never writes to another terminal.

A consuming check marks the batch it returns as handled, so the next check returns newer mail; no --ack is needed. Several --wait calls may wait on one inbox; waiting reserves nothing, listeners woken by the same arrival get the same Delivery, and --ack of a handled Delivery is a no-op. Consuming checks belong to the agent itself. A script that only watches the inbox must use --peek (including --peek --wait) and must never --ack, or it takes mail the agent never sees. If a check response was lost, rerun it with the --retry-request it printed to get the same batch. To find mail after losing context, run orca orchestration inbox --terminal <mailbox> --limit <n> --full and name the mailbox: run:<run_id> for a coordinator's bound Run, or dispatch:<dispatch_id> for a worker, including mail it read before it bound a helper Run.

commands.summary: Create a decision gate blocking a task

notes: --run inspects a named Run without binding; otherwise gates are scoped to the caller.

commands.summary: Create and bind a lightweight orchestration Run
notes: A Run is a namespace and home inbox. It never schedules or places workers. worker-start --spec creates one when none is bound; use run-create for Task graphs or a new goal.
--retry-request is only for exact recovery after an unknown mutation result.
Valid --type values: status, dispatch, worker_done, merge_ready, escalation, handoff, decision_gate, question, heartbeat.
To answer a worker question, use orchestration reply --id <msg_id> --body <text> with the same Orca CLI executable.
Group addresses (@all, @idle, @codex, ...) reach the live Dispatches of your own Run; a sender in no Run must use run:<id> or dispatch:<id>. @worktree:<id> names one workspace.

Run groups exclude their owning coordinator; send to run:<id> to raise something with yours. Nested coordinators receive group mail in their child Run mailbox; @worktree:<id> includes workspace coordinators.
On Windows PowerShell, quote group addresses such as --to "@all" or --to "@worktree:<id>".
worker_done and heartbeat are exact-Dispatch signals and cannot target groups; omit --to to use the Dispatch's Run mailbox.
worker_done requires --outcome succeeded or --outcome failed.
From a worker, an omitted recipient defaults to its coordinator, also after it finished; mail sent after finishing, worker_done included, leaves the finished task unchanged.
Use --to dispatch:<id> for attempt-specific coordinator guidance; Orca durably relays it to a connected worker server.

A worker_done with the active task/dispatch IDs completes that task only from the dispatched pane. When stable pane identity is unavailable, the sender handle must exactly match the dispatch assignee; injected preambles include the correct --from value.
Prefer --task-id/--dispatch-id/etc. over raw --payload JSON in worker commands; PowerShell strips JSON quotes easily.

--on <server> mails a terminal or chat agent on a paired server (--to term_… or orca_session_id:…). Your own Orca carries it, and replies come back to your own check. From an agent, --environment runs the command on that server and delivers no mail.
A Dispatch created by orchestration dispatch is shown as unsupervised and reports the exact adopted terminal when its identity is still provable.

observation.agentWait names a worker parked on a prompt only a human can answer, with the evidence that proved it (hook, prompt-text, or title). Null means Orca looked and found no wait. An absent field means it never looked — an older host, an unverifiable worker identity, an unreadable pane, or an agent probe that did not answer in time — and never means the worker is not waiting. A waiting worker is healthy, not failed.

commands.summary: Start one supervised worker on the Run home or a connected Orca server
notes: With --spec and no bound Run, a coordinator gets a new Run bound to it, named after the Task title; the receipt names the Run it created or joined.
Current and existing worktrees never rerun setup; a fresh agent terminal is created unless --terminal is explicit.
When reusing --terminal, pass --worktree for that terminal; current means the coordinator worktree.
Reusing a settled worker's terminal with --terminal before its autoReleaseAt cancels that automatic release; after it, the start is refused while the release runs.
A terminal the user kept open takes --terminal work and stays kept open.
--agent takes an Orca agent id enabled on the worker server, such as claude, codex, cursor, antigravity, muse, zcode, opencode, or opencode2.

--model supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, Grok, and Muse opaque provider model ids; --effort requires --model. OMP also takes its model roles and selectors (such as @worker or provider/model:level), with --effort as its thinking level. Neither can combine with --terminal. OpenCode model selection requires an existing worktree, a verified execution-host CLI, and an available model; effort is unsupported. Other agents, including zcode, launch with the model from their own config.
Finished workers close on their own unless started with --keep-open; a worker started in a new worktree (new-child or new-top-level) is kept open, so release it when no one will use its chat.

New worktrees use agent-first creation; without --setup, setup runs unless the project turns it off. Repository start-immediately runs setup beside the agent; wait-for-setup gates agent readiness and task input.
New worktrees without --name get the name Orca gives an unnamed workspace; the receipt names it. Servers older than this change still require --name.

Creation flags (--name, --repo, --base-branch, --display-name, --comment, --setup) are rejected for current/existing worktrees. Use exact --repo on the selected server; project/host convenience routing remains on worktree create.

How the worker runs follows the user's own setting for new agent tabs; there is no flag for it and no caller needs to ask. A dispatch the setting cannot apply to still starts, so the placement, agent, and launch options passed here are always the ones honoured.

Drive every worker the same way whichever way it was started: the same orchestration verbs, the same handle. Mail, dispatch, worker-show, worker-read and the whole lifecycle behave identically. The start receipt records which one ran, for operators and telemetry.

Not every worker has a terminal. Read output with worker-read --source auto or --source transcript, which always work; --source terminal is refused when there is none, and orca terminal verbs do not accept every worker handle. Nothing above needs you to know which kind you have — the orchestration verbs cover all of them.
--on selects only the worker server; the Run and this command remain on the current Orca server.

With --on, use an exact remote selector, new-child or new-top-level (new-child and new-top-level need a remote --repo); new-child nests the server worktree under your workspace, or starts it top-level with a warning when that server is too old to nest across machines. Remote current is invalid.
--retry-of needs --task naming the failed Task (--spec creates a new one) and does not inherit placement; repeat the intended --on/worktree and --agent/terminal choices.
--spec-file reads the spec from a file (relative to the current directory) or stdin (-) on this machine, so quotes and backticks need no shell escaping.
--keep-open keeps the worker open after it finishes, as worker-keep-open does right after start.

The call exits 0 for ready, and in the concise view for a start whose turn was not yet observed (--full exits 1 for anything but ready). Failed or outcome_unknown exits 1 and JSON includes stage/failedStage, setup, effects, residualResources, and recovery commands when needed.
caller.orcaSessionId is this agent's Orca session ID, as Orca resolved it, when the agent runs as an Orca session; otherwise caller is omitted.

commands.summary: Create a terminal session in the current worktree
notes: Creates a visible terminal tab without switching focus when possible; falls back to a background handle if the UI cannot adopt it. Pass --focus to switch to it.
This creates a terminal and runs --command in it. To start an agent, use `orca agent launch` (or `orca worktree create --agent` for a new checkout), which follows your Chat | CLI choice.

--shell picks the shell the terminal IS on a Windows host (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, wsl.exe, bash.exe, git-bash); --command is typed into whatever shell the host started, so `--command cmd.exe` leaves a cmd running INSIDE the default shell and exiting it drops back to that shell.

A host that cannot apply --shell refuses the create rather than quietly spawning its default shell: macOS and Linux execution hosts spawn the login shell, terminals routed over SSH resolve their shell on the SSH host, a --shell that contradicts the project execution runtime (WSL vs Windows host) is refused, and an Orca host older than --shell is refused by the CLI.
